budget_items.what_was_said: As an alternative to payment in lieu, the board discussed requiring a rising percentage of units be affordable as development size increases.
Using an assumed sale price and the draft 2% payment-in-lieu rate, a member calculated what a nine-unit development would pay the town, and compared it to what it costs to build a house.
The board re-ran the payment-in-lieu math at a higher percentage to see if it came closer to the value of a home, and considered doubling the draft rate.

what_happened.line: Planning Board reviewed second drafts of cluster, senior, and inclusionary zoning bylaws aimed at the May 2027 town meeting, taking no substantive votes.
The board asked for payment-in-lieu percentages to be recalculated by development-size tier for the next draft of the inclusionary bylaw.
A bylaw change affecting dwelling-unit counts on common driveways was tabled until the state legislature acts on a possible statewide duplex-by-right mandate.
The board asked the building inspector for an opinion on whether the existing inclusionary bylaw applies to the Parmiter Road development.
The board set a plan to brief other town boards individually and hold a fall public forum, favoring the library or senior center over the high school as venue.

why_it_matters: These zoning bylaws, if placed on the warrant, would go to voters at the May 2027 annual town meeting and could change what developers must pay or build for affordable units.
The payment-in-lieu percentage under revision affects how much money the town collects from housing developments in place of built affordable units.
Whether the inclusionary bylaw is found to apply to the Parmiter Road development could determine affordable-unit requirements for a project already in progress.
watch_next: Town counsel's input on the inclusionary bylaw draft, expected before the 24th
A fall public forum on the draft bylaws, before the May 2027 town meeting warrant
